indicators.note: one piece is said to be filled in by another, so the second goes inside the first

parts.note: something discretionary is left to choice, i.e. optional
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A clock-watcher notes that hours are padded out when work is done at one's own discretion.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine that is working is functioning, in service, up and running.

parts.note: a mission is a task or piece of work one is sent to do

explanation.surface: An old piece of work has been left untended.
explanation.definitionFit: Neglect, the failure to do something, is a synonym of leaving it out.

indicators.note: cooked means prepared or doctored, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: the name with its S kept as letters for the mix
taken as written

explanation.surface: A remarkable pie baked by a man called Alec.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' rearranges the eight letters ALECS plus PIE.
explanation.definitionFit: Notable and special both describe something out of the ordinary, deserving particular attention.

clue.text: Endlessly sanction a place in Scotland

indicators.note: endlessly says the last letter of the word for sanction is dropped

parts.note: to sanction something is to allow it

explanation.surface: Officials keep authorising a visit to somewhere north of the border.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endlessly' cuts the W from ALLOW. ALLOA is a small town in central Scotland, on the Forth.
explanation.definitionFit: Alloa is a Scottish town in Clackmannanshire, so it is one particular place there.

clue.text: Scotsman protects princess from the Middle East

indicators.note: one piece protects another by surrounding it, so the second goes inside

parts.note: Ian is the Scottish form of John, a typical Scotsman's name
a rani is an Indian queen or princess

explanation.surface: A Scotsman shields a princess who has come from the Middle East.
explanation.walkthrough: Ian is the Scottish form of John, so it stands for any Scotsman.
explanation.definitionFit: Iran is in the Middle East, so a person from there is described by the adjective formed from it.

parts.note: nigh means nearly or almost
to tie something is to fasten or secure it

explanation.surface: Someone checks that their clothing is nearly fastened.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightdress is an item of clothing, here clothing in the sense of a garment.

clue.text: Picture shows lights on the promontory

parts.note: to light on something is to land or alight on it, so lights means lands
a cape is a headland or promontory

explanation.surface: A painting shows lights shining on a headland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lights' reads as lamps, but it is the verb: a bird lights, or lands, on a branch.
explanation.definitionFit: A landscape is a painting or photograph of scenery, so a kind of picture.

indicators.note: endlessly says the word's final letter is lost

parts.note: to pickle meat or fish is to cure it

explanation.surface: A villain finds himself in a pickle that never ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' drops the last letter from CURE.
explanation.definitionFit: Cur is an old insult for a contemptible man, a synonym for a scoundrel.

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for commanding officer
to be up on a subject is to be well informed, knowledgeable
on means concerning or about, as in a talk on history

explanation.surface: An officer is well informed about a voucher.
explanation.definitionFit: A coupon is a ticket or slip exchanged for a discount, i.e. a voucher.

definitions.note: 15 refers to the answer to 15-across, a test; this is a verb phrase

indicators.note: unhappily suggests the word is in a bad state, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sister is miserable that she must sit the paper a second time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unhappily' rearranges SISTER; 15 is the clue for the paper at 15-across.
explanation.definitionFit: Students who fail a test sit it a second time: the verb for retaking.

clue.text: Force politician to wear Hawaiian garland back to front

indicators.note: a garland is worn round the neck, so the politician goes inside it
back to front says the garland's word is read in reverse

parts.note: a lei is a Hawaiian garland of flowers
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A politician is made to put on a Hawaiian flower necklace, wrongly turned round.
explanation.walkthrough: The garland must be turned round before the politician goes in; reversing after the insertion gives the wrong letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To impel someone is to drive or compel them, a synonym of force as a verb.

indicators.note: a spilled liquid is scattered, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Seamen knock over a bottle of Angostura bitters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Argonauts were Jason's crew aboard the Argo in Greek myth, hence sailors.

parts.note: a social is a party or gathering
1st, written with the digit read as I, abbreviates first

explanation.surface: A member of the Fabian Society always gives priority to the party.
explanation.walkthrough: The Fabian Society is a British left-wing group, so a Fabian is one of its members.
explanation.definitionFit: The Fabian Society promotes gradual left-wing reform, so a Fabian is one kind of leftist.

parts.note: in bridge the four players are North, East, South and West, so S
port is the left-hand side of a ship

explanation.surface: A card player walks out on a game of bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: A sport is a competitive game or pastime.

clue.text: Working to keep proportion in speech

indicators.note: one piece keeps another by holding it, so the second goes inside

parts.note: a device switched on is working
a ratio is a proportion between quantities

explanation.surface: A busy speaker keeps a sense of proportion in a speech.
explanation.definitionFit: An oration is a formal speech, delivered on a ceremonial occasion.

clue.text: In dialect translation is the same

indicators.note: translation renders words into another form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Something rendered from a regional dialect comes out unchanged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'translation' rearranges IN plus DIALECT; 'is' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Identical means exactly alike, with no difference between the two things.

parts.note: ex means former, as the late holder of an office is the former one
a.m. stands for ante meridiem, the morning

explanation.surface: A morning newspaper arrives late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'paper' looks like a newspaper here, but it is a test paper.
explanation.definitionFit: An examination paper is a written test, so paper serves as a synonym.

clue.text: Some years with conservation group that's corrupt

parts.note: a decade is a period of ten years
NT is the National Trust, the British heritage conservation body

explanation.surface: A heritage charity is accused of years of corruption.
explanation.walkthrough: The National Trust looks after historic houses and countryside in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Decadent describes moral decline and self-indulgence, close to corrupt or debased.

clue.text: Advocate is to concede, having absorbed conclusion

indicators.note: a piece that absorbs another takes it inside itself

parts.note: to defer to someone is to yield or concede
an end is a conclusion

explanation.surface: A lawyer agrees to give way once the case has reached its end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is to' only links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A defender is one who speaks up for a person or cause, a champion or advocate.

indicators.note: one piece engulfs another by swallowing it whole, so the second goes inside

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland

explanation.surface: A river floods a valley in the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engulfs' puts N inside DEE; a dene is a narrow wooded valley in British dialect.
explanation.definitionFit: Dene is a regional British word for a small, often wooded, valley.

parts.note: ex means former, as the late chairman is the former one
to claim is to demand something as one's right

explanation.surface: Someone rings late and starts insisting on things.
explanation.definitionFit: To exclaim is to cry out or call suddenly, as in surprise.

clue.text: Go in front making president withdraw

parts.note: to recede is to move back or withdraw

explanation.surface: Someone forces the president to stand down so they can lead.
explanation.definitionFit: To precede is to come or go before something in order or position.

parts.note: Peru is a South American country, with its possessive S
Al is the chemical symbol for aluminium

explanation.surface: A scientist closely studies one of a nation's chemical elements.
explanation.definitionFit: A perusal is a thorough reading or inspection of something.

parts.note: a let is an obstruction or hindrance, as in without let or hindrance
Prince Hal is Shakespeare's name for the young Henry V

explanation.surface: Fatal limits are imposed on a prince.
explanation.definitionFit: Lethal means causing death, an exact synonym of deadly.

indicators.note: one piece goes aboard another, getting inside it

parts.note: dingy means dirty, drab, grimy

explanation.surface: A husband climbs into a dirty boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A dinghy is a small boat, so a type of vessel.

clue.text: Point to reference book, shortly to become law

parts.note: E is east, one of the compass points
dict. is the short form of dictionary

explanation.surface: Someone directs us to a dictionary, saying it will soon have legal force.
explanation.definitionFit: An edict is an official decree or order with legal force.

clue.text: Show flashes of brilliance when resolving court case

indicators.note: resolving breaks something down and settles it anew, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A lawyer dazzles everyone while settling a lawsuit.
explanation.definitionFit: To coruscate is to sparkle or flash, and figuratively to be dazzlingly clever.

clue.text: Spilt the beans about money in a manner of speaking

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: to sing is ... for informing, so sang means spilt the beans
L stands for pound, the British unit of money, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Someone blabbed about cash, figuratively speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts L inside SANG; 'in a' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang is an informal vocabulary, a particular way of talking.

clue.text: Superior found drunk with college girl

parts.note: high means intoxicated
a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: A snob is found intoxicated with a female student.
explanation.definitionFit: High-class means of superior quality or social standing.

indicators.note: one piece is in another, so it is placed inside

parts.note: an ad is a commercial or advertisement
men means people, as in the men and women of a town

explanation.surface: People appearing in an advertisement want to change it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' only links; the commercial alone supplies the outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To amend is to alter or modify, especially a text, so to change it.

definitions.meaning: to put something down or place it
a short narrative poem or ballad, meant to be sung

explanation.definitionFit: Lay is both a verb for placing something and an old word for a ballad.

clue.text: Predicament harboured by inadequate old council worker

indicators.note: one piece harboured by another is sheltered inside it

parts.note: lame means weak or inadequate, so lamer is more so
a plight is a difficult situation or predicament

explanation.surface: A difficult situation is concealed by a feeble former municipal employee.
explanation.walkthrough: Lamplighters went round lighting gas street lamps for local councils, hence 'old'.
explanation.definitionFit: Before electric street lighting, a municipal employee went round lighting gas lamps each evening.
